questions.scenario: You are trying to teach your grandparents how to use WhatsApp or UPI (Paytm). What do you do?

options.text: I physically hold their phone and show them exactly which button to tap and where it goes.
I ask them what exactly confuses them—is the text too small or the buttons hard to find?
I tell them to just look for the 'Green Phone Icon' or the 'Blue Tick' to make it visually easy.
I set up the app for them, link the bank account, and manage their daily limits safely.

questions.scenario: You open Swiggy or Zomato to order a burger, but the app is very confusing today.

options.text: I keep clicking different menus and swiping around until I finally find the checkout page.
I get annoyed and think, 'Why did they hide the cart button? That's terrible user experience.'
I ignore the confusing buttons and just look at the mouth-watering food photos.
I switch to another app immediately because I don't want to waste time struggling.

questions.scenario: Your school asks you to make a PowerPoint presentation for a science project.

options.text: I add cool animations, transitions, and clickable links to make it feel like a real app.
I make sure the fonts are readable from the back bench and the information flows logically.
I spend 80% of my time choosing the perfect color theme, aesthetic fonts, and HD images.
I delegate the design work to a friend and focus on presenting it perfectly to the teacher.

questions.scenario: You are organizing your smartphone's home screen.

options.text: I arrange apps based on how my thumb naturally moves so I can open them fast.
I put my most-used apps on the first page and delete the ones I haven't used in 30 days.
I download aesthetic icon packs, widgets, and matching wallpapers to make it look beautiful.
I put all apps in specific labeled folders like 'Productivity', 'Games', and 'Social'.

questions.scenario: When you buy a new electronic gadget or a smart watch, how do you learn to use it?

options.text: I just turn it on and start pressing all the buttons to see what happens.
I read the manual or watch a detailed YouTube review about its hidden features.
I mostly care about changing the watch faces and customizing the screen colors.
I set it up quickly to track my daily steps and manage my notifications efficiently.

questions.scenario: You and your friends are deciding which new game to play on your phones.

options.text: I care about how smooth the controls are and if the character moves perfectly.
I read the Play Store reviews to see if people are complaining about bugs or lag.
I choose the game that has the highest quality graphics and coolest 3D environments.
I look at the size of the game and if it has annoying unskippable ads before downloading.

questions.scenario: Your school diary/planner looks like this:

options.text: Full of quick scribbles, folded pages, and sticky notes everywhere for fast access.
Divided logically into sections so I can track my homework and test dates perfectly.
Decorated with doodles, highlighters, and aesthetic calligraphy on every page.
Used purely to list down my daily tasks and cross them out when finished.

questions.scenario: You visit an ATM to withdraw cash, but the screen menu is very old and confusing.

options.text: I quickly memorize the button sequence so I don't have to read it next time.
I observe how elderly people struggle with it and think of ways to make it simpler.
I cringe at the ugly blue pixelated screen and terrible 90s fonts.
I just get my money as fast as possible and leave before the line gets long.

questions.scenario: If you had to design a completely new app for Indian students, what would be your main focus?

options.text: Making sure the swipe gestures and buttons feel super satisfying to use.
Interviewing 50 students to find out exactly what their biggest daily problem is.
Creating a stunning Dark Mode UI with neon colors and a modern logo.
Figuring out how to get 10,000 downloads in the first month and monetizing it.

questions.scenario: When someone shows you their newly designed website, what is your first comment?

options.text: 'The drop-down menu is a bit laggy, let's fix that.'
'The text is too small to read on a mobile phone, users will leave.'
'The colors look premium, but the font doesn't match the vibe.'
'Where is the Buy Now button? We need to increase the sales conversions.'

Interactive_Prototyper.title: Interaction Designer / Prototyper
Interactive_Prototyper.primary_match_text: You are a hands-on builder! You care about how things actually work, move, and feel when someone interacts with them.
Interactive_Prototyper.day_in_the_life: Building clickable prototypes of apps, adding smooth swipe animations, and testing if the buttons actually work.
Interactive_Prototyper.alternative_match_text: Your love for building interactive things also makes you a great fit for Frontend Web Development or Game Design.
Interactive_Prototyper.roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th (PCM is a bonus). Pursue a B.Des in Interaction Design or B.Tech/BCA.

UX_Researcher.title: UX Researcher / Usability Analyst
UX_Researcher.primary_match_text: You are the psychologist of the design world. You love observing human behavior, finding flaws, and making things easier for people to use.
UX_Researcher.day_in_the_life: Interviewing users, watching them struggle with an app, and finding logical solutions to improve the experience.
UX_Researcher.alternative_match_text: Because of your deep understanding of human psychology, you would also excel in Psychology or Product Management.
UX_Researcher.roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th (Humanities/Science). Pursue a B.Des, BA in Psychology, or specialized UX Research courses.

UI_Visual_Designer.title: UI / Visual Designer
UI_Visual_Designer.primary_match_text: You are highly aesthetic and creative! You have a natural eye for colors, typography, and making digital things look premium and beautiful.
UI_Visual_Designer.day_in_the_life: Choosing the perfect color palettes, designing icons, and creating stunning, high-quality app screens on Figma.
UI_Visual_Designer.alternative_match_text: Your strong aesthetic sense makes you a perfect candidate for Graphic Design, Animation, or Art Direction.
UI_Visual_Designer.roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th (Arts with Drawing is great). Pursue a B.Des in Communication Design or Graphic Arts.

Design_Manager.title: Product Design Manager
Design_Manager.primary_match_text: You are a strategic thinker. You care about aesthetics, but you care more about the final goal—whether the design actually drives business and growth.
Design_Manager.day_in_the_life: Managing a team of designers, presenting the app to investors, and ensuring the design increases the company's profit.
Design_Manager.alternative_match_text: With your leadership and strategic mindset, you would easily thrive as a Product Manager or Startup Founder.
Design_Manager.roadmap: Commerce or Science in 11th/12th. Pursue a BBA, B.Des, or B.Tech followed by an MBA.
